speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Sit, Master Shakespeare, while the broth still has a skin of heat. Threepence is the meal. I will not have it eaten standing.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have an hour before Shoreditch. The settle is welcome. Errors at two, and I am the old father in it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Look at the board before you dip. Two fingers short of the notch, and a penny still. The notch is the one my husband cut. The penny has not heard about the notch.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: The loaf was light at the baker's this morning as well, Mistress. I did not argue the price. The price was the penny.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Advent, and two fingers gone, and I am not opening a parliament about wheat. Alse, the salt, and then your hands still.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Is it Saturday they play the two lovers? I have heard the walking, upstairs, since before the frost.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Saturday at two, if the yard can stand the cold. I am not selling you a seat. I have not been asked for one.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Is there a moon in it? I should like a moon, if there is going to be a dark part.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: There is a moon they call for, and it does not always come. That is as much as I am telling at a table.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Hold your tongue about Saturday, girl. A playhouse in December is a draught with a price on it. Fetch the small beer.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I only asked after a moon.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: And you have had your answer, which was not a promise. Beer.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The meal is threepence, Mistress. The sixpence is the week's firing and washing, and it runs to Lady Day. I am not paying the firing again because I sat down.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Threepence on the slate for the broth and the short loaf. The sixpence is its own line, and it is not this bowl. I can tell a meal from a week. Mark me.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: I am at the loom till the bell, Mistress. If the bolt is to stay off, I will say so before I change the hour.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Say it, and the bolt stays. I ask that of any man under these tiles, and of no man a speech about his work.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have one roll to copy after Egeon. My own dips. I will not burn yours past what the sixpence already buys.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then we understand each other. Eat. Gib is on the third stair again, and I will not have a player and a cat in the same fall.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: (the jug set down) I will not ask again about Saturday. I asked about the moon. That was the question.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: That was the question. Thank you for the beer.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: A good afternoon at the play, Master Shakespeare.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: And you at the loom, Gillis.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Three pence. Two fingers. A penny. Go and be an old father, and do not bring the playhouse home on your shoes.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will scrape them. God keep this kitchen.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The slate has threepence and nothing else. Shut it behind you.
